territorial_scope.description: Applies to sales and upgrades of new passenger vehicles under a California statute.

evidence.quote: A dealer or manufacturer shall not sell any new passenger vehicle

summary.short: Adds Vehicle Code §24011.5: manufacturers and dealers must give buyers a distinct notice naming and describing the functions and limitations of any SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature, and may not market such features as implying autonomous capability. The text states no start date.
summary.long: Adds Vehicle Code §24011.5. Subdivision (a) bars dealers and manufacturers from selling a new passenger vehicle equipped with a partial driving automation feature, or providing an update that adds one, unless the buyer or owner receives a distinct notice at delivery or upgrade naming the feature and describing its functions and limitations. Subdivision (b) bars naming or marketing such features in ways that imply autonomous capability or functions not actually included; a violation is a misleading advertisement under Vehicle Code §11713. Subdivision (c) defines the covered features by reference to SAE Level 2 in J3016 (April 2021). Subdivision (d) preserves existing duties of care and civil liability. Subdivision (e) requires manufacturers to give dealers information, including recommended notice language, before delivery, on which dealers may rely; subdivision (f) shields manufacturers that provide it when a dealer fails to give notice. Section 2 states no state reimbursement is required for local agencies or school districts. The text gives no effective date and no penalty amounts beyond the §11713 cross-reference.

thresholds.note: The text sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its scope turns on the category 'Level 2 partial driving automation' defined by reference to SAE J3016 (April 2021), which is a classification rather than a number. The remaining figures are cross-references and the standard's edition date, not thresholds.
